$comment: G7 canary fixtures (plan §6). Release-facing claims captured from the trees that falsified them, quoted verbatim (row 9 is the one condensation, flagged in its own `origin`; rows 22, 24 and 26 are the excerpts, flagged the same way). EIGHT capture waves, declared in `captureWaves` and named per row by `wave` — there is no single fixture-wide commit: rows 1-2 are pre-framework-slim, rows 3-9 are the pre-single-entry `root-full` family, rows 10-20 are what the core convergence commit itself left behind (rows 10-11, 16 and 17-20 pre-date it and were falsified by it; rows 12-15 its token-level rewrite minted), and rows 21 onward are the per-package pairs the wrapper and next convergences collapsed — 21-22 react, 23-24 vue, 25-26 solid, 27-28 next, 29-31 svelte. Rows 17-20 were captured by the exhaustive-closure round: 17 proves the modal `root entry … is absent` wording, and 18-20 the three costumes of the same claim that never say the word `root` — the dist file name, `the core entry out`, and a bare `without either`. With them EVERY alternative of the `root-free` family is proved against the exact sentence it exists to kill. The per-package rows do the same for their own families, and most follow one shape: the odd row is the literal retired specifier or identifier, the even row is the claim it enabled, quoted as an excerpt that deliberately starts AFTER the specifier so the costume that never names it is proved on its own. The costume differs per package because the hazard did — react's is its React context object, vue's is `I18N_INJECTION_KEY` (the `Symbol("i18n")` a second build pass duplicated), solid's is its solid context, and next's pair is a second host-constructor name plus a size/matrix ladder named after a tier that no longer exists. Svelte takes THREE rows rather than two: `svelte-package` preserves modules, so both svelte specifiers always resolved to the same binding modules and that package never had the two-context hazard at all. Its false claim was instead that mixing the two entries is merely wasteful, a sentence that survives the specifier being stripped out of it, so it needs a canary of its own — and the third row is the sentence that used to fence the react family from `mutations`, moved here once the svelte family made it fire by design. The G7 gate FAILS unless its pattern set matches ALL of them, which is what proves the patterns work against the exact claims they exist to kill; it also fails if a row's `wave` does not resolve, because a canary that cannot say where it came from sends the next reader to the wrong tree. `mutations` is the other half of that proof and runs under the same scan: each row is a TRUE claim, and the gate fails if ANY pattern fires on it — `mustNotMatch` names the family a row was minted to fence, but the assertion is over the WHOLE set, so every row fences every family. The fence CHANGED SHAPE at the wrapper convergences and the reason is worth keeping. While `/slim` subpaths were live, a package-scoped family was fenced by a sibling's sentence: a pattern that could not tell `@comvi/react/slim` from `@comvi/vue/slim` would have reported live entries as stale. P3 and P4 retired the last of those, so no sibling specifier is available to fence with, and the rows were re-pointed accordingly. What survives the whole wave is the word `slim` in prose that is CORRECT: the permanent `pnpm codemod:framework-slim` invocation, and the changeset FILENAMES the rewritten-in-place entries keep (`react-framework-slim.md`, `vue-single-package-slim.md`, `solid-framework-slim.md`, `svelte-framework-slim.md`, `next-single-package-slim.md` and their siblings), which live prose cites by name. Every package-scoped family is therefore anchored on the retired SPECIFIER or IDENTIFIER, never on the bare word, and the mutation rows are the proof. Two rows quote bundler-matrix case names (`react-on-slim`, `react-slim-preset`) that the react convergence retired into `react-default` and `react-icu`; the text stays byte-identical because a canary is a snapshot of what a file said at a commit, never a pointer to a live case. This file is NOT part of the G7 corpus (scripts/ is out of scope), so it cannot self-collide. Never edit the text: it is a historical snapshot, not documentation. SINGLE-ENTRY P6 activated the two GLOBAL families the plan holds back until the whole corpus is false (§8.9, "P6 enables the global forms and re-counts the corpus"), and the rows above were re-pointed rather than re-captured — no canary TEXT changed, because a canary is a snapshot of what a file said at a commit and the claims it quotes did not move. What changed is which family owns each claim. The four package-scoped `/slim` families lost their SPECIFIER half to one global rule, `slim-host-subpath` (`@comvi/<any>/slim`), because the fence that forced the scoping is gone: while sibling `/slim` entries were live, a pattern that could not tell `@comvi/react/slim` from `@comvi/vue/slim` would have reported live entries as stale, and P3/P4 retired the last sibling. So rows 21, 23, 25, 29 and 31 — the five that quote a specifier — now name `slim-host-subpath`, and what remains of each package family is its COSTUME half, renamed for the claim it actually catches: `react-two-contexts`, `vue-two-injection-keys`, `solid-two-contexts`, `svelte-two-specifiers` (rows 22, 24, 26, 30). Row 28's `next-stale-ladder` likewise became the global `stale-ladder`, covering every wrapper's retired size row and matrix case rather than next's alone. Two structural additions on the negative side. (1) `mustNotMatch` is now VALIDATED against the declared pattern names, as `mustMatch` always was implicitly: a fence pointed at a family that a rename dissolved reports nothing, and four of these rows would have become exactly that. (2) A mutation row may declare `sanctioned[]` — the one family whose design is "fire on EVERY occurrence and let the allowlist pin the reviewed ones" is `slim-host-subpath`, so row 4, the scream changeset's `@comvi/core/slim` sentence, asserts in both directions: that family MUST fire (which is also the only proof that the global rule reaches CORE's retired specifier, a thing no package-scoped family ever did) and every other pattern still must not. Six negatives were added: the root README's one-entry-per-package table, whose `@comvi/core` row legitimately writes the same specifier in both columns and is what pins the `|` exclusion in `same-specifier-hosts`; core's live capability subpaths, which the generalised specifier rule must not reach; the "absorbed the old `react-on-slim` case" idiom, which is the only thing keeping `stale-ladder`'s retired-qualifier lookbehind honest; and the react, solid and svelte successor sentences, each one word away from the costume canary it replaced.
